newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-DE LA HOYA TAKES NEW TRAINER TO GET PUNCH BACK.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-DE LA HOYA TAKES NEW TRAINER TO GET PUNCH BACK.

text.p: Oscar De La Hoya has turned to veteran trainer Emanuel Steward to put the punch back into his game for his World Boxing Council welterweight title defence against David Kamau next month.

"I just thought by bringing in Emanuel Steward that he would bring back my offence that I was lacking in my last couple of fights," De La Hoya said in a teleconference call on Thursday from his training camp in Big Bear, California, where he has been preparing with Steward for the June 14 bout in San Antonio.
For his last six bouts De La Hoya (24-0) had been trained by Jesus "The Professor" Rivero and had used a more defensive approach. De La Hoya's last knockout was of Darryl Tyson 15 months ago.

In his last two fights, De La Hoya went the 12-round distance to beat Mexican Miguel Angel Gonzalez and then again to win a unanimous decision against Pernell Whitaker on April 12 to take the welterweight crown.
De La Hoya has shown power in the past and thoroughly beat up legendary Mexican champion Julio Cesar Chavez last June before stopping him in the fourth round.
Steward is best known as the trainer for Thomas "Hit Man' Hearns, the hard hitting five-time world champion who made his mark in the 1980s.

"He is very smart, you can see what he did for Thomas Hearns," De La Hoya said of Steward, who is also working with WBC heavyweight champion Lennox Lewis for his July 12 title defence against fellow Briton Henry Akinwande.

"I know I have the left hook," said De La Hoya, 24. "The right hand, that is something I have to work on. Hearns had a beautiful right hand, Emaneul Steward can teach me what he taught Thomas Hearns."
Now with Steward in his corner, De La Hoya says he wants to knockout Kamau, 28-1, whose only loss was to Chavez two years ago.
"For this fight I want to get the knock out," De La Hoya said of next month's bout at the Alamodome.
Not only is De La Hoya ready for a knockout win now, but he feels it is a must as he looks ahead to fighting against harder hitting, bigger foes.

"I want these guys to respect me," De La Hoya said of possible future opponents. "If I knockout Kamau clean I will gain my respect back. That is really what I want. We are up in the ring, if a fighter doesn't get respect from an opponent it might be trouble."
The only person who will be in trouble next month will be Kamau according to De La Hoya.

"He is very vulnerable to the right, that's why we are working on the right hand," De La Hoya said. "He keeps his guard so high that shots to the body will bring his hands down right away and then you go to the head."
